newsitem.title: JAPAN: Father of crash survivor says daughter unhurt.
newsitem.headline: Father of crash survivor says daughter unhurt.

text.p: The father of an 11-year-old Japanese girl who survived the crash of a Korean Air Lines Co (KAL) jumbo jet said on Wednesday his daughter only suffered slight injuries and sounded fine over the phone.
"I was able to talk to her. She sounded all right," Tatsuo Matsuda told reporters at his home in Shizuoka Prefecture, 150 km (94 miles) west of Tokyo.
But Matsuda said he was worried about his wife, Shigeko, 44, who urged their daughter, Rika, to leave first before escaping the plane herself.
"According to Rika, my wife followed her out, but we haven't received any confirmation yet," Matsuda said. Rika and Shigeko were sitting near the rear of the plane.

Guam Governor Carl Gutierrez, one of the first people to reach the crash scene, said he rescued five people, including Rika, but flames stopped him from going back into the wreckage to save her mother.
"The mother was dead in the flames," Gutierrez said.
The mother and daughter were on a sightseeing trip to Guam after visiting Shigeko's family in Seoul. Matsuda left for Seoul in the afternoon to meet his wife's family before heading for Guam.
The 747 jumbo jet crashed on the U.S. Pacific island of Guam, killing more than 200 people. Thirty people survived, including some who walked away from burning wreckage.

The jumbo jet was flying from Seoul to Guam, carrying mostly South Korean tourists and honeymooners, when it crashed in heavy rain and ruptured an oil pipeline just miles from the airport. The cause of the crash is still unknown.
